records.context: **Offsets are solved globally, never accumulated.** Chaining microscope image field-to-microscope image field shifts along a row of a 10x10 grid adds every pairwise error together, so the last microscope image field lands tens of pixels out with nothing in the output saying so. Instead every overlapping neighbour pair contributes one equation ``p_j - p_i = d_ij`` and the whole set is solved at once as a weighted least-squares problem over the pair graph (see :func:`solve_positions`). Redundant edges — the diagonal neighbours of a grid, the ``i``/``i+2`` pairs of a heavily-overlapped row — then *cancel* error instead of compounding it, and each microscope image field gets a **residual**: how far its solved position sits from what its own pairs asked for. A large residual is the signal that a microscope image field did not register, and it is written into the table rather than averaged away.
records.label: spacr.align#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Offsets are solved globally, never accumulated.** Chaining tile-to-tile shifts along a row of a 10x10 grid adds every pairwise error together, so the last tile lands tens of pixels out with nothing in the output saying so. Instead every overlapping neighbour pair contributes one equation ``p_j - p_i = d_ij`` and the whole set is solved at once as a weighted least-squares problem over the pair graph (see :func:`solve_positions`). Redundant edges — the diagonal neighbours of a grid, the ``i``/``i+2`` pairs of a heavily-overlapped row — then *cancel* error instead of compounding it, and each tile gets a **residual**: how far its solved position sits from what its own pairs asked for. A large residual is the signal that a tile did not register, and it is written into the table rather than averaged away.
records.translation: **Los desplazamientos se resuelven globalmente, nunca se acumulan.** Encadenar desplazamientos de tesela a tesela a lo largo de una fila de una cuadrícula de 10x10 suma todos los errores por pares, de modo que la última tesela acaba decenas de píxeles desplazada sin que nada en la salida lo indique. En su lugar, cada par de vecinos solapados aporta una ecuación ``p_j - p_i = d_ij`` y todo el conjunto se resuelve de una vez como un problema de mínimos cuadrados ponderados sobre el grafo de pares (véase :func:`solve_positions`). Las aristas redundantes — los vecinos diagonales de una cuadrícula, los pares ``i``/``i+2`` de una fila muy solapada — *cancelan* entonces el error en lugar de acumularlo, y cada tesela recibe un **residuo**: cuánto se aleja su posición resuelta de lo que pedían sus propios pares. Un residuo grande es la señal de que una tesela no se registró, y se escribe en la tabla en lugar de diluirse en un promedio.

records.context: **A pair that does not register is reported, not guessed.** Phase correlation over a blank or near-empty overlap returns a confident-looking peak that is pure noise. Every pair is therefore scored by the normalised cross-correlation of the two strips *after* the measured shift is applied; below ``min_confidence`` the pair is dropped, and a microscope image field left with no surviving pair keeps its nominal stage position and is marked ``method='nominal'``. A nominally-placed microscope image field is not the same thing as a registered one and :data:`ALIGN_TABLE` says which is which, per microscope image field.
records.label: spacr.align#8
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A pair that does not register is reported, not guessed.** Phase correlation over a blank or near-empty overlap returns a confident-looking peak that is pure noise. Every pair is therefore scored by the normalised cross-correlation of the two strips *after* the measured shift is applied; below ``min_confidence`` the pair is dropped, and a tile left with no surviving pair keeps its nominal stage position and is marked ``method='nominal'``. A nominally-placed tile is not the same thing as a registered one and :data:`ALIGN_TABLE` says which is which, per tile.
records.translation: **Un par que no se registra se notifica, no se adivina.** La correlación de fase sobre un solapamiento en blanco o casi vacío devuelve un pico de apariencia fiable que es puro ruido. Por eso cada par se puntúa con la correlación cruzada normalizada de las dos franjas *después* de aplicar el desplazamiento medido; por debajo de ``min_confidence`` el par se descarta, y una tesela que se queda sin ningún par superviviente conserva su posición nominal de la platina y se marca con ``method='nominal'``. Una tesela colocada nominalmente no es lo mismo que una registrada, y :data:`ALIGN_TABLE` indica cuál es cuál, tesela a tesela.

records.context: **Image data channels share one solution.** Registration runs on ``reference_channel`` alone and the resulting placement is applied to every image data channel of that site. Aligning image data channels independently would shear the composite — a nucleus mask and its own DAPI image data channel would no longer line up — so it is not offered.
records.label: spacr.align#9
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Channels share one solution.** Registration runs on ``reference_channel`` alone and the resulting placement is applied to every channel of that site. Aligning channels independently would shear the composite — a nucleus mask and its own DAPI channel would no longer line up — so it is not offered.
records.translation: **Los canales comparten una solución.** El registro se ejecuta solo sobre ``reference_channel`` y la colocación resultante se aplica a todos los canales de esa posición. Alinear los canales de forma independiente deformaría la composición — una máscara de núcleos y su propio canal DAPI dejarían de coincidir —, así que no se ofrece.

records.source: A "site" is a position on the stage, not a file. records.context: the image layer registration is measured on. Every image data channel of a site then shares that site's single solution — registering image data channels independently would shear the composite. ``None`` (the default) takes the image data channel the microscope image fields already carry, which is the one :func:`scan_tiles` selected. This used to default to ``0``, so ``scan_tiles(reference_channel=2)`` followed by the documented ``estimate_offsets(tiles)`` silently registered on image data channel 0 instead — the selection was stored on every microscope image field and read by nothing. Microscope image fields that disagree fall back to ``0``; the resolved value is recorded on the plan and printed by :func:`format_plan`, so whichever way it went is visible rather than assumed.
records.label: spacr.align.estimate_offsets#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: the plane registration is measured on. Every channel of a site then shares that site's single solution — registering channels independently would shear the composite. ``None`` (the default) takes the channel the tiles already carry, which is the one :func:`scan_tiles` selected. This used to default to ``0``, so ``scan_tiles(reference_channel=2)`` followed by the documented ``estimate_offsets(tiles)`` silently registered on channel 0 instead — the selection was stored on every tile and read by nothing. Tiles that disagree fall back to ``0``; the resolved value is recorded on the plan and printed by :func:`format_plan`, so whichever way it went is visible rather than assumed.
records.translation: el plano sobre el que se mide el registro. Después, todos los canales de una posición comparten la única solución de esa posición — registrar los canales de forma independiente deformaría la composición. ``None`` (el valor por defecto) toma el canal que ya llevan las teselas, que es el que seleccionó :func:`scan_tiles`. Antes el valor por defecto era ``0``, de modo que ``scan_tiles(reference_channel=2)`` seguido del ``estimate_offsets(tiles)`` documentado registraba en silencio sobre el canal 0 — la selección se guardaba en cada tesela y nada la leía. Las teselas que discrepan recurren a ``0``; el valor resuelto se registra en el plan y lo imprime :func:`format_plan`, de modo que lo ocurrido queda a la vista en lugar de suponerse.

records.context: Each edge ``(i, j, dy, dx, w)`` contributes one weighted equation ``p_j - p_i = (dy, dx)``; each tile contributes one weak equation ``p_i = nominal_i``. Minimising the whole residual at once is what stops error accumulating.

records.source: Each edge ``(i, j, dy, dx, w)`` contributes one weighted equation ``p_j - p_i = (dy, dx)``; each tile contributes one weak equation ``p_i = nominal_i``. Minimising the whole residual at once is what stops error accumulating.
records.translation: Cada arista ``(i, j, dy, dx, w)`` aporta una ecuación ponderada ``p_j - p_i = (dy, dx)``; cada tesela aporta una ecuación débil ``p_i = nominal_i``. Minimizar todo el residuo de una vez es lo que impide que el error se acumule.

records.context: **Why accumulation fails.** Adding every measured shift to the previous position gives ``p_k = sum(d_0..d_k)`` and carries each measurement error forward. Ten tiles with 0.3 px errors place the last tile 3 px away from its correct position. Least squares distributes errors across *identical input measurements*. A real grid has redundant edges, including the tile below, the tile to the right, and the ``i``/``i+2`` pairs in a heavily overlapped row. Their disagreements can cancel instead of accumulating. The returned per-tile residual records the remaining disagreement.
records.label: spacr.align.solve_positions#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Why not accumulate.** Walking a row and adding each measured shift to the previous position gives ``p_k = sum(d_0..d_k)``, so every measurement error is carried forward: ten tiles with 0.3 px errors put the last one 3 px out, and nothing in the output says so. Least squares over the *same* measurements distributes the error instead — and because a real grid has redundant edges (the tile below as well as the tile to the right, or the ``i``/``i+2`` pairs of a heavily overlapped row), disagreements cancel rather than compound. The surviving disagreement is the per-tile residual, which is returned.
records.translation: **Por qué no acumular.** Recorrer una fila sumando cada desplazamiento medido a la posición anterior da ``p_k = sum(d_0..d_k)``, de modo que cada error de medición se arrastra: diez teselas con errores de 0.3 px dejan la última desplazada 3 px, y nada en la salida lo indica. Los mínimos cuadrados sobre las *mismas* mediciones reparten, en cambio, el error — y como una cuadrícula real tiene aristas redundantes (la tesela de abajo además de la de la derecha, o los pares ``i``/``i+2`` de una fila muy solapada), las discrepancias se cancelan en lugar de acumularse. La discrepancia que queda es el residuo por tesela, que se devuelve.

records.context: Seams are **feathered**: each microscope image field's contribution is weighted by a linear ramp that rises from the microscope image field edge inward over :attr:`AlignPlan.feather` pixels, and the band is divided by the total weight. A hard cut would leave a straight, high-contrast edge exactly where two microscope fields of view meet — and a straight edge is the single most reliable thing a downstream segmentation will find and call an object boundary. Feathering costs one extra float32 image layer per band and makes the join a gradient instead. ``blend='average'`` weights every contributor equally and ``blend='none'`` is last-writer-wins, both kept mainly so the difference can be measured.
records.label: spacr.align.write_stack#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Seams are **feathered**: each tile's contribution is weighted by a linear ramp that rises from the tile edge inward over :attr:`AlignPlan.feather` pixels, and the band is divided by the total weight. A hard cut would leave a straight, high-contrast edge exactly where two fields meet — and a straight edge is the single most reliable thing a downstream segmentation will find and call an object boundary. Feathering costs one extra float32 plane per band and makes the join a gradient instead. ``blend='average'`` weights every contributor equally and ``blend='none'`` is last-writer-wins, both kept mainly so the difference can be measured.
records.translation: Las costuras se **difuminan**: la contribución de cada tesela se pondera con una rampa lineal que sube desde el borde de la tesela hacia dentro a lo largo de :attr:`AlignPlan.feather` píxeles, y la franja se divide por el peso total. Un corte brusco dejaría un borde recto y de alto contraste justo donde se juntan dos campos — y un borde recto es lo que con más fiabilidad encontrará una segmentación posterior y tomará por el límite de un objeto. El difuminado cuesta un plano float32 adicional por franja y convierte la unión en un gradiente. ``blend='average'`` pondera igual a todos los contribuyentes y ``blend='none'`` deja que prevalezca el último en escribir; ambos se conservan sobre todo para poder medir la diferencia.

records.context: ``NAN_DROP_FEATURES`` drop any feature column containing a NaN. On a real database it often removes every ``pathogen_*`` column, because those columns are NaN for cells without a pathogen. ``NAN_DROP_OBJECTS`` drop any object row containing a NaN. Usually removes almost everything, for the same reason; offered because on a single-object-type export it is often exactly right. ``NAN_ZERO`` / ``NAN_MEAN`` impute. records.translation: ``NAN_DROP_FEATURES`` descarta cualquier columna de características que contenga un NaN. En una base de datos real a menudo elimina todas las columnas ``pathogen_*``, porque esas columnas son NaN para las células sin patógeno. ``NAN_DROP_OBJECTS`` descarta cualquier fila de objeto que contenga un NaN. Suele eliminar casi todo, por la misma razón; se ofrece porque en una exportación de un solo tipo de objeto a menudo es exactamente lo correcto. ``NAN_ZERO`` / ``NAN_MEAN`` imputan. Ambas escriben por defecto una máscara booleana ``layers['missing']`` de la misma forma, para que los valores imputados puedan distinguirse de los medidos; la máscara booleana cuesta 1 byte por celda frente a 4 para el ``float32`` de ``X`` por defecto.

records.context: This module is also the authority on **what an extracted-image-region PNG on disk means** -- see the "Crop PNG format" section below. In short: the current format is 3 ("declared_rgb", :data:`CROP_FORMAT_CURRENT`), whose red, green and blue slots hold exactly the source image data channels ``settings['png_channel_mapping']`` names; format 1 ("legacy", unmarked) holds the same bytes for the default mapping and is returned untouched; format 2, written for eleven days in 2026, is the one that is reversed, and :func:`read_crop_png` is what reverses it back. A folder says which format it is via a ``.spacr_crop_format.json`` sidecar, and an unmarked folder is format 1.
records.label: spacr.crops#11
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: This module is also the authority on **what a crop PNG on disk means** -- see the "Crop PNG format" section below. In short: the current format is 3 ("declared_rgb", :data:`CROP_FORMAT_CURRENT`), whose red, green and blue slots hold exactly the source channels ``settings['png_channel_mapping']`` names; format 1 ("legacy", unmarked) holds the same bytes for the default mapping and is returned untouched; format 2, written for eleven days in 2026, is the one that is reversed, and :func:`read_crop_png` is what reverses it back. A folder says which format it is via a ``.spacr_crop_format.json`` sidecar, and an unmarked folder is format 1.
records.translation: Este módulo es también la autoridad sobre **lo que significa un PNG de recorte en disco** -- véase la sección "Crop PNG format" más abajo. En resumen: el formato actual es el 3 ("declared_rgb", :data:`CROP_FORMAT_CURRENT`), cuyas ranuras roja, verde y azul contienen exactamente los canales de origen que indica ``settings['png_channel_mapping']``; el formato 1 ("legacy", sin marca) contiene los mismos bytes para la asignación por defecto y se devuelve intacto; el formato 2, escrito durante once días de 2026, es el invertido, y :func:`read_crop_png` es lo que lo vuelve a invertir. Una carpeta indica su formato mediante un archivo auxiliar ``.spacr_crop_format.json``, y una carpeta sin marca es de formato 1.

records.translation: :func:`spacr.measure.measure_crop` escribe un PNG por objeto para cada objeto que mide (``<root>/data/.../{cell,nucleus,pathogen,cytoplasm}_png/``) y registra las rutas en la tabla ``png_list`` de ``measurements/measurements.db``. records.translation: Primero van los canales de intensidad (el subconjunto seleccionado por ``settings['channels']`` en el preprocesamiento) y después un plano de máscara de etiquetas ``uint16`` por cada clase de objeto segmentada, siempre en el orden **célula, núcleo, patógeno, orgánulo** -- cada uno presente solo si esa clase se segmentó. ``settings['cell_mask_dim']`` / ``nucleus_mask_dim`` / ``pathogen_mask_dim`` / ``organelle_mask_dim`` registran los índices de plano resultantes; la disposición por defecto de cuatro canales de spaCR es ``{cell: 4, nucleus: 5, pathogen: 6, organelle: 7}`` (:data:`DEFAULT_MASK_DIMS`).

records.context: :func:`extract_crop` reproduces the PNG path in ``spacr.measure._measure_crop_core`` step for step: same image data channel selection (``png_dims``), same region definition (object mask, optionally replaced by its padded bounding box, optionally dilated), same ``_crop_center`` centering/padding, same ``normalize_to_dtype`` percentile normalisation, same dtype. :func:`png_view` turns that array into what a consumer sees after the PNG round trip, and :func:`read_crop_png` reads an extracted-image-region PNG back into the same thing -- the two are the two halves of one contract, and ``tests/test_crops.py`` asserts they agree.

records.source: :func:`extract_crop` reproduces the PNG path in ``spacr.measure._measure_crop_core`` step for step: same channel selection (``png_dims``), same region definition (object mask, optionally replaced by its padded bounding box, optionally dilated), same ``_crop_center`` centering/padding, same ``normalize_to_dtype`` percentile normalisation, same dtype. :func:`png_view` turns that array into what a consumer sees after the PNG round trip, and :func:`read_crop_png` reads a crop PNG back into the same thing -- the two are the two halves of one contract, and ``tests/test_crops.py`` asserts they agree.
records.translation: :func:`extract_crop` reproduce paso a paso la ruta de PNG de ``spacr.measure._measure_crop_core``: la misma selección de canales (``png_dims``), la misma definición de región (máscara del objeto, opcionalmente sustituida por su rectángulo delimitador con margen y opcionalmente dilatada), el mismo centrado/relleno de ``_crop_center``, la misma normalización por percentiles de ``normalize_to_dtype`` y el mismo dtype. :func:`png_view` convierte ese array en lo que ve un consumidor tras el viaje de ida y vuelta por PNG, y :func:`read_crop_png` vuelve a leer un PNG de recorte en lo mismo -- ambas son las dos mitades de un mismo contrato, y ``tests/test_crops.py`` comprueba que coinciden.

Re-anchoring goes through :func:`reanchor_path`, so it is separator-agnostic (a Windows path opened on Linux re-anchors), it takes the LAST ``<folder>`` component rather than the first (an old root that itself contained a ``data`` folder used to produce a path naming a directory), and "already under the root" is a component-wise prefix test rather than a substring one. records.source: a row carrying ``png_path`` (or ``path``), or a bare path string, which is accepted as-is and only re-anchored. A row with neither raises :class:`CropError`. Re-anchoring goes through :func:`reanchor_path`, so it is separator-agnostic (a Windows path opened on Linux re-anchors), it takes the LAST ``<folder>`` component rather than the first (an old root that itself contained a ``data`` folder used to produce a path naming a directory), and "already under the root" is a component-wise prefix test rather than a substring one. A path carrying no anchor at all is returned untouched even if it points nowhere on this machine, and the failure surfaces on read.
records.translation: una fila que incluye ``png_path`` (o ``path``), o una cadena de ruta simple, que se acepta tal cual y solo se vuelve a anclar. Una fila sin ninguno de los dos lanza :class:`CropError`. El reanclaje pasa por :func:`reanchor_path`, por lo que no depende del separador (una ruta de Windows abierta en Linux se reancla), toma el componente ``<folder>`` LAST (último) en lugar del primero (una raíz antigua que contenía a su vez una carpeta ``data`` producía antes una ruta que nombraba un directorio), y "already under the root" (ya bajo la raíz) es una prueba de prefijo por componentes y no de subcadena. Una ruta sin ningún anclaje se devuelve intacta aunque no apunte a ningún sitio en esta máquina, y el fallo aparece al leer.

Object-specific values in nested ``png_size``, ``dialate_pngs``, and ``dialate_png_ratios`` are selected by the object's position in ``crop_mode`` and fall back to the first entry when that object is absent. Channels are resolved from ``png_channel_mapping``, or legacy ``png_dims``, through :func:`channels_from_settings` and stored in colour order. Text forms such as ``"[2, 98]"``, ``"2,98"``, and ``"[1 99]"`` are parsed as percentile windows; a non-text sequence with a length other than two disables normalization.
records.translation: Los ajustes de ``measure_crop``. Un ``png_size`` escalar define un recorte cuadrado. Los valores específicos de cada objeto en ``png_size``, ``dialate_pngs`` y ``dialate_png_ratios`` anidados se seleccionan según la posición del objeto en ``crop_mode`` y recurren a la primera entrada cuando ese objeto no está. records.context: A machine-learning classification model trained on legacy extracted image regions learned "input image layer 0 is whatever is in the file's red image data channel", and in a legacy file that is ``png_dims[-1]``. Feed the same model a format-2 extracted image region and image layer 0 is now ``png_dims[0]`` -- a permutation of its input, which the model scores without throwing an error and classifies incorrectly.
records.label: spacr.crops.legacy_channel_names#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: A classifier trained on legacy crops learned "input plane 0 is whatever is in the file's red channel", and in a legacy file that is ``png_dims[-1]``. Feed the same model a format-2 crop and plane 0 is now ``png_dims[0]`` -- a permutation of its input, which the model scores without raising an error and classifies incorrectly.
records.translation: Un clasificador entrenado con recortes heredados aprendió que "input plane 0 is whatever is in the file's red channel" (el plano de entrada 0 es lo que haya en el canal rojo del archivo), y en un archivo heredado eso es ``png_dims[-1]``. Si se da al mismo modelo un recorte de formato 2, el plano 0 pasa a ser ``png_dims[0]`` -- una permutación de su entrada, que el modelo puntúa sin lanzar ningún error y clasifica incorrectamente.

records.context: Reversing the request undoes the permutation exactly: red and blue swap, green is unmoved. So a model trained with ``train_channels=['r','g','b']`` keeps seeing the pixels it was trained on if it is applied with ``['b','g','r']``, and one trained with ``['r','g']`` with ``['b','g']``.

records.translation: Invertir la solicitud deshace exactamente la permutación: el rojo y el azul se intercambian y el verde no se mueve. Así, un modelo entrenado con ``train_channels=['r','g','b']`` sigue viendo los píxeles con los que se entrenó si se aplica con ``['b','g','r']``, y uno entrenado con ``['r','g']``, con ``['b','g']``.

records.context: :func:`build_png_channels` assembles the extracted image region in **file order** -- red plane first -- while ``cv2.imwrite`` interprets a 3-image data channel array as BGR. Reversing the image data channel axis here, once, in the writer, makes cv2's interpretation land the array's red plane in the file's red slot, so the PNG's slots hold the image data channels ``settings['png_channel_mapping']`` named (format 3). records.source: :func:`build_png_channels` assembles the crop in **file order** -- red plane first -- while ``cv2.imwrite`` interprets a 3-channel array as BGR. Reversing the channel axis here, once, in the writer, makes cv2's interpretation land the array's red plane in the file's red slot, so the PNG's slots hold the channels ``settings['png_channel_mapping']`` named (format 3). Under :data:`DEFAULT_PNG_CHANNEL_MAPPING` that puts ``png_dims[0]`` in blue, byte-identical to format 1.
records.translation: :func:`build_png_channels` ensambla el recorte en **el orden del archivo** -- primero el plano rojo --, mientras que ``cv2.imwrite`` interpreta un array de 3 canales como BGR. Invertir aquí el eje de canales, una sola vez, en el escritor, hace que la interpretación de cv2 coloque el plano rojo del array en la ranura roja del archivo, de modo que las ranuras del PNG contienen los canales que nombró ``settings['png_channel_mapping']`` (formato 3). Con :data:`DEFAULT_PNG_CHANNEL_MAPPING`, esto pone ``png_dims[0]`` en el azul, idéntico byte a byte al formato 1.

records.context: This module maps an **arbitrary external schema** onto spaCR's and guards against these silent failures:
records.label: spacr.foreign#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: This module maps an **arbitrary external schema** onto spaCR's and guards against these silent failures:
records.translation: Este módulo hace corresponder un **esquema externo arbitrario** con el de spaCR y protege frente a estos fallos silenciosos:

records.context: 1. **A guessed mapping applied without review.** Their ``Area`` in µm² written into spaCR's ``cell_area`` in px² is a number that is wrong by a factor of a few hundred and looks completely plausible. So :func:`infer_column_map` only ever *proposes*; the proposal is a file the user edits (:func:`save_column_map` / :func:`load_column_map`); and :func:`run_import` applies what was agreed, nothing else. 2. **Units.** spaCR's intensities are raw uncalibrated counts, and its geometry is px²/px for a 2-D run — but a 3-D run measures volumes, in µm³ when it was given voxel_size_z_um/voxel_size_xy_um, under the same column names; the row's ``measurement_units`` says which, and :mod:`spacr.feature_dict` resolves it per table. A foreign table in µm needs a scale factor unless the target rows are µm too, and every mapping therefore carries ``unit_in`` / ``unit_out``. When a conversion is declared but the pixel size is unknown, the value is **not** multiplied by 1.0 and pretended to be pixels: the column is redirected to the ``foreign_`` prefix, recorded with its own unit and ``calibrated = 0``, and named in the plan and the summary. 3. **Columns that could not be mapped.** They are listed by name in the plan, in :meth:`ImportResult.summary`, and in the ``foreign_columns`` table — and they are still *imported*, under the ``foreign_`` prefix. No column is dropped silently. 4. **Name collisions.** A foreign column called ``cell_area`` that means something else would corrupt every downstream analysis with no error at all. Targets are checked against :func:`spacr.feature_dict.parse_column` and against spaCR's reserved identifier columns; a collision is a :class:`Conflict` that either refuses the import (``on_conflict='refuse'``, the default) or renames the column (``on_conflict='rename'``) — never an overwrite. 5. **A destination that is already somebody's project.** The same argument one level up: a *table* collision. See below.

So :func:`infer_column_map` only ever *proposes*; the proposal is a file the user edits (:func:`save_column_map` / :func:`load_column_map`); and :func:`run_import` applies what was agreed, nothing else. 2. **Units.** spaCR's intensities are raw uncalibrated counts, and its geometry is px²/px for a 2-D run — but a 3-D run measures volumes, in µm³ when it was given voxel_size_z_um/voxel_size_xy_um, under the same column names; the row's ``measurement_units`` says which, and :mod:`spacr.feature_dict` resolves it per table. A foreign table in µm needs a scale factor unless the target rows are µm too, and every mapping therefore carries ``unit_in`` / ``unit_out``. When a conversion is declared but the pixel size is unknown, the value is **not** multiplied by 1.0 and pretended to be pixels: the column is redirected to the ``foreign_`` prefix, recorded with its own unit and ``calibrated = 0``, and named in the plan and the summary. 3. **Columns that could not be mapped.** They are listed by name in the plan, in :meth:`ImportResult.summary`, and in the ``foreign_columns`` table — and they are still *imported*, under the ``foreign_`` prefix. No column is dropped silently. 4. **Name collisions.** A foreign column called ``cell_area`` that means something else would corrupt every downstream analysis with no error at all. Targets are checked against :func:`spacr.feature_dict.parse_column` and against spaCR's reserved key columns; a collision is a :class:`Conflict` that either refuses the import (``on_conflict='refuse'``, the default) or renames the column (``on_conflict='rename'``) — never an overwrite. 5. **A destination that is already somebody's project.** The same argument one level up: a *table* collision. See below.
records.translation: 1. **Una correspondencia adivinada aplicada sin revisión.** Su ``Area`` en µm² escrita en el ``cell_area`` de spaCR en px² es un número erróneo en un factor de unos cientos que parece totalmente plausible. Por eso :func:`infer_column_map` solo *propone*; la propuesta es un archivo que edita el usuario (:func:`save_column_map` / :func:`load_column_map`); y :func:`run_import` aplica lo acordado y nada más. 2. **Unidades.** Las intensidades de spaCR son recuentos brutos sin calibrar, y su geometría está en px²/px en una ejecución 2-D — pero una ejecución 3-D mide volúmenes, en µm³ cuando se le dieron voxel_size_z_um/voxel_size_xy_um, con los mismos nombres de columna; el ``measurement_units`` de la fila indica cuál, y :mod:`spacr.feature_dict` lo resuelve por tabla. Una tabla externa en µm necesita un factor de escala salvo que las filas de destino también estén en µm, y por eso cada correspondencia lleva ``unit_in`` / ``unit_out``. Cuando se declara una conversión pero se desconoce el tamaño de píxel, el valor **no** se multiplica por 1.0 fingiendo que son píxeles: la columna se redirige al prefijo ``foreign_``, se registra con su propia unidad y ``calibrated = 0``, y se nombra en el plan y en el resumen. 3. **Columnas que no pudieron hacerse corresponder.** Se enumeran por nombre en el plan, en :meth:`ImportResult.summary` y en la tabla ``foreign_columns`` — y aun así se *importan*, con el prefijo ``foreign_``. Ninguna columna se descarta en silencio. 4. **Colisiones de nombres.** Una columna externa llamada ``cell_area`` que signifique otra cosa corrompería todo análisis posterior sin ningún error. Los destinos se comprueban con :func:`spacr.feature_dict.parse_column` y con las columnas clave reservadas de spaCR; una colisión es un :class:`Conflict` que o bien rechaza la importación (``on_conflict='refuse'``, el valor por defecto) o bien renombra la columna (``on_conflict='rename'``) — nunca sobrescribe. 5. **Un destino que ya es el proyecto de alguien.** El mismo argumento un nivel más arriba: una colisión de *tablas*. Véase más abajo.

records.translation: ``run_import`` copia la tabla importada en la tabla canónica ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` cuando no hay nada de nadie más en ella, para que un proyecto construido solo por importación sea legible por todas las herramientas de spaCR. records.context: The ranked set is the table's, not the drop's. ``table`` stores which token owns which column in :attr:`FieldTable.channel_tokens`, and a later drop is ranked against the union of what it brings and what is already there. Ranking each drop on its own instead would put a second microscope field of view's ``C2`` in column 0 beside a first microscope field of view's ``C1``, and the only sign of it would be in the database.

records.context: **3-D requires a z/xy relationship and will not invent one.** With anisotropic voxels an unspaced volume is not merely in unusual units: a voxel count is not proportional to a physical volume, a distance transform measures a different length along z than along x, and ``major_axis_length`` mixes the two. records.context: Args: png_channels (ndarray): The extracted image region in file order -- red image layer first -- as :func:`spacr.crops.build_png_channels` assembles it. Written without narrowing, so a ``uint16`` extracted image region becomes a 16-bit PNG; a float extracted image region is silently written as 8-bit by cv2. Four or more image data channels raise rather than losing one to an alpha image layer. img_path (str): Where the PNG goes. Its parent folder is stamped with the format sidecar and **must already exist** -- the caller in ``_measure_crop_core`` creates it. If it does not, the stamp fails with a printed warning, ``cv2.imwrite`` returns False, and the call returns normally having written nothing at all. A bare filename with no directory part stamps the current working directory. grid (list): Anything with ``append``; read only when ``plot`` is true, and appended to in place, so the return value is the object that was passed in. ``None`` passes through untouched while ``plot`` is false. plot (bool): Truthiness, not identity, decides. False (the default) leaves ``grid`` completely untouched -- the PNG is still written -- which is why an ordinary run ends with an empty grid. True appends the extracted image region for :func:`img_list_to_grid`: an extracted image region of exactly dtype ``uint16`` is appended as a high-byte narrowed ``uint8`` copy, every other dtype is appended unchanged, and a ``uint8`` extracted image region is appended by reference, so a caller that reuses its buffer mutates what is already in the grid.

records.source: Args: png_channels (ndarray): The crop in file order -- red plane first -- as :func:`spacr.crops.build_png_channels` assembles it. Written without narrowing, so a ``uint16`` crop becomes a 16-bit PNG; a float crop is silently written as 8-bit by cv2. Four or more channels raise rather than losing one to an alpha plane. img_path (str): Where the PNG goes. Its parent folder is stamped with the format sidecar and **must already exist** -- the caller in ``_measure_crop_core`` creates it. If it does not, the stamp fails with a printed warning, ``cv2.imwrite`` returns False, and the call returns normally having written nothing at all. A bare filename with no directory part stamps the current working directory. grid (list): Anything with ``append``; read only when ``plot`` is true, and appended to in place, so the return value is the object that was passed in. ``None`` passes through untouched while ``plot`` is false. plot (bool): Truthiness, not identity, decides. False (the default) leaves ``grid`` completely untouched -- the PNG is still written -- which is why an ordinary run ends with an empty grid. True appends the crop for :func:`img_list_to_grid`: a crop of exactly dtype ``uint16`` is appended as a high-byte narrowed ``uint8`` copy, every other dtype is appended unchanged, and a ``uint8`` crop is appended by reference, so a caller that reuses its buffer mutates what is already in the grid.
records.translation: Args: png_channels (ndarray): El recorte en el orden del archivo -- primero el plano rojo -- tal como lo ensambla :func:`spacr.crops.build_png_channels`. Se escribe sin reducir la profundidad, de modo que un recorte ``uint16`` se convierte en un PNG de 16 bits; cv2 escribe en silencio un recorte float como de 8 bits. Cuatro o más canales lanzan un error en lugar de perder uno en un plano alfa. img_path (str): Dónde se guarda el PNG. Su carpeta padre se marca con el archivo auxiliar de formato y **debe existir ya** -- la crea quien llama en ``_measure_crop_core``. Si no existe, la marca falla con una advertencia impresa, ``cv2.imwrite`` devuelve False y la llamada termina normalmente sin haber escrito nada. Un nombre de archivo sin parte de directorio marca el directorio de trabajo actual. grid (list): Cualquier objeto con ``append``; solo se lee cuando ``plot`` es verdadero, y se amplía in situ, de modo que el valor devuelto es el objeto que se pasó. ``None`` pasa sin cambios mientras ``plot`` es falso. plot (bool): Decide su valor de verdad, no su identidad. False (el valor por defecto) deja ``grid`` completamente intacto -- el PNG se sigue escribiendo -- y por eso una ejecución normal termina con una cuadrícula vacía. True añade el recorte para :func:`img_list_to_grid`: un recorte cuyo dtype es exactamente ``uint16`` se añade como copia ``uint8`` reducida al byte alto, cualquier otro dtype se añade sin cambios, y un recorte ``uint8`` se añade por referencia, de modo que quien llama y reutiliza su búfer modifica lo que ya está en la cuadrícula.

records.translation: Los recortes siguen siendo ``uint16``, así que son PNG de 16 bits y no se descarta ninguna intensidad al escribir. records.context: **GUI-only, deliberately.** It passes ``cli_note`` and no ``entry``, so ``spacr-run power`` answers with :data:`APP_CLI_NOTE` instead of "unknown module". Every other ``spacr-run`` module takes a ``src`` and processes it; this one takes a design, and its output is a curve you read by comparing points on it. records.translation: **Solo para la GUI, deliberadamente.** Pasa ``cli_note`` y ningún ``entry``, de modo que ``spacr-run power`` responde con :data:`APP_CLI_NOTE` en lugar de "unknown module" (módulo desconocido). La razón no es que el barrido no pueda ejecutarse sin interfaz — puede, y la nota nombra la llamada —, sino que sus *entradas* no son un archivo de configuración. Todos los demás módulos de ``spacr-run`` reciben un ``src`` y lo procesan; este recibe un diseño, y su salida es una curva que se lee comparando sus puntos. Un settings.csv que fijara un único punto de esa curva sería una interfaz peor para :func:`spacr.power_model.scan_parameters` que llamarla directamente, que es exactamente lo que la nota indica al usuario.

If the code line says ``+ rowID + columnID``, ρ and γ are here; if the plate-position toggle turns them off, BOTH lose them; if they are random effects, both say random. A box whose two formulas disagree is worse than a box with one.
records.translation: Las matemáticas y el código deben coincidir, y esta es la mitad que los mantiene de acuerdo: recibe los mismos dos argumentos de placa que :func:`formula_for` y los interpreta igual. records.translation: Las ranuras de orgánulo las resuelve :mod:`spacr.organelle_types`, que es dueño de la nomenclatura de ranuras: los prefijos llevan letras -- ``organelle``, ``organelleb``, ... -- y ``organelle`` es prefijo de todos los demás, así que la coincidencia debe probarse de más larga a más corta y corresponde al lugar donde se generan los nombres, en lugar de escribirse por segunda vez aquí.

It is rank deficient, so its individual coefficients are not uniquely interpretable. :data:`COLLINEAR_FORMULA` stores the formula used by the compatibility checks.
records.translation: Los efectos de guía y de gen se describen como ajustes separados. El diseño retirado, ``y ~ fraction:grna + gene_fraction:gene + rowID + columnID``, contiene tanto las fracciones de las guías como sus sumas a nivel de gen. Es de rango deficiente, por lo que sus coeficientes individuales no son interpretables de forma única. :data:`COLLINEAR_FORMULA` guarda la fórmula que usan las comprobaciones de compatibilidad.

records.context: Timelapse first generates masks for a time series and then links adjacent frames. The costs differ greatly: segmenting twelve frames with Cellpose takes tens of seconds, while relinking *the twelve existing label images* with a new ``timelapse_displacement`` takes milliseconds. The preview separates these stages so a slider change does not rerun segmentation:
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.timelapse_preview#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The Timelapse module is mask generation over a time series followed by frame-to-frame linking. Those two halves cost wildly different amounts: segmenting twelve frames with Cellpose is tens of seconds, re-linking the *same* twelve label images with a new ``timelapse_displacement`` is milliseconds. A preview that re-segments on every slider move is unusable, so this panel splits them:
records.translation: El módulo Timelapse es la generación de máscaras sobre una serie temporal seguida del enlace entre fotogramas. Esas dos mitades cuestan cantidades muy distintas: segmentar doce fotogramas con Cellpose lleva decenas de segundos, mientras que volver a enlazar las *mismas* doce imágenes de etiquetas con un nuevo ``timelapse_displacement`` lleva milisegundos. Una vista previa que vuelve a segmentar con cada movimiento del deslizador es inutilizable, así que este panel las separa:

records.context: **The sequence is read lazily.** :class:`FrameSequence` never materialises the whole time series: a directory reads one file at a time, a multi-page TIFF reads one page at a time, and an ``.npy`` stack is memory-mapped and sliced. Only the frames the preview actually shows are touched, and a small LRU keeps the scrubber responsive without pinning the movie in RAM.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.timelapse_preview#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **The sequence is read lazily.** :class:`FrameSequence` never materialises the whole time series: a directory reads one file at a time, a multi-page TIFF reads one page at a time, and an ``.npy`` stack is memory-mapped and sliced. Only the frames the preview actually shows are touched, and a small LRU keeps the scrubber responsive without pinning the movie in RAM.
records.translation: **La secuencia se lee de forma diferida.** :class:`FrameSequence` nunca materializa toda la serie temporal: un directorio se lee archivo a archivo, un TIFF de varias páginas página a página, y una pila ``.npy`` se mapea en memoria y se trocea. Solo se tocan los fotogramas que la vista previa muestra realmente, y una pequeña caché LRU mantiene ágil la barra de desplazamiento sin retener la película en RAM.

records.context: What the panel *shows* is chosen around the two failure modes people actually tune a tracker against:
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.timelapse_preview#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: What the panel *shows* is chosen around the two failure modes people actually tune a tracker against:
records.translation: Lo que *muestra* el panel se elige en función de los dos modos de fallo frente a los que realmente se ajusta un seguidor:

records.context: **Fragmentation** — one object becoming several track ids. Surfaced as track count, mean/median track length, the number of tracks shorter than a live-settable N, and the count of tracks that start after the first frame or end before the last one.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.timelapse_preview#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Fragmentation** — one object becoming several track ids. Surfaced as track count, mean/median track length, the number of tracks shorter than a live-settable N, and the count of tracks that start after the first frame or end before the last one.
records.translation: **Fragmentación** — un objeto que se convierte en varios ids de trayectoria. Se muestra como el número de trayectorias, la longitud media/mediana de las trayectorias, el número de trayectorias más cortas que un N ajustable en directo, y el recuento de trayectorias que empiezan después del primer fotograma o terminan antes del último.

records.context: **Identity swaps** — a track jumping to a different object. Surfaced as the number of within-track steps longer than the displacement limit the user is tuning, plus the largest single step. Masks are relabelled *by track id* and drawn in a per-track colour, so a swap is visible as an object changing colour mid-movie.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.timelapse_preview#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Identity swaps** — a track jumping to a different object. Surfaced as the number of within-track steps longer than the displacement limit the user is tuning, plus the largest single step. Masks are relabelled *by track id* and drawn in a per-track colour, so a swap is visible as an object changing colour mid-movie.
records.translation: **Intercambios de identidad** — una trayectoria que salta a otro objeto. Se muestra como el número de pasos dentro de una trayectoria más largos que el límite de desplazamiento que el usuario está ajustando, más el mayor paso individual. Las máscaras se reetiquetan *por id de trayectoria* y se dibujan con un color por trayectoria, de modo que un intercambio se ve como un objeto que cambia de color a mitad de la película.

records.context: The module provides three things for a workflow processing session:
records.label: spacr.runctx#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The module provides three things for a pipeline run:
records.translation: El módulo proporciona tres cosas para una ejecución de pipeline:

records.context: **One processing-session id, on every log line and every output.** :func:`run_context` mints one id, stamps it onto every :class:`logging.LogRecord` created anywhere in the process, writes a per processing session JSONL log that :func:`read_run_log` reads back, and hands the *same* id to :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. A log line and an output can therefore be joined on ``run_id``, so every log record of the processing session that produced a given file can be retrieved.
records.label: spacr.runctx#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **One run id, on every log line and every output.** :func:`run_context` mints one id, stamps it onto every :class:`logging.LogRecord` created anywhere in the process, writes a per-run JSONL log that :func:`read_run_log` reads back, and hands the *same* id to :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. A log line and an output can therefore be joined on ``run_id``, so every log record of the run that produced a given file can be retrieved.
records.translation: **Un id de ejecución, en cada línea de registro y en cada salida.** :func:`run_context` genera un id, lo estampa en cada :class:`logging.LogRecord` creado en cualquier parte del proceso, escribe un registro JSONL por ejecución que :func:`read_run_log` vuelve a leer y entrega el *mismo* id a :func:`spacr.artifacts.register_run_outputs`. Así, una línea de registro y una salida pueden unirse por ``run_id``, de modo que se pueden recuperar todos los registros de la ejecución que produjo un archivo dado.

records.context: **One seed for every random number generator.** :func:`seed_everything` seeds Python, NumPy (legacy global *and* the :class:`~numpy.random.Generator` stream :func:`spacr_rng` hands out), Torch on CPU and every CUDA device, and — through those two — Cellpose, so field shuffling, fold splits and Cellpose initialisation repeat between runs with the same seed. sklearn has no global seed at all; :func:`random_state` is what estimator construction sites pass. What cannot be made deterministic is listed in :attr:`SeedReport.caveats` and in :func:`seed_everything`'s docstring.
records.label: spacr.runctx#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **One seed for every random number generator.** :func:`seed_everything` seeds Python, NumPy (legacy global *and* the :class:`~numpy.random.Generator` stream :func:`spacr_rng` hands out), Torch on CPU and every CUDA device, and — through those two — Cellpose, so field shuffling, fold splits and Cellpose initialisation repeat between runs with the same seed. sklearn has no global seed at all; :func:`random_state` is what estimator construction sites pass. What cannot be made deterministic is listed in :attr:`SeedReport.caveats` and in :func:`seed_everything`'s docstring.
records.translation: **Una semilla para todos los generadores de números aleatorios.** :func:`seed_everything` siembra Python, NumPy (el global heredado *y* el flujo :class:`~numpy.random.Generator` que reparte :func:`spacr_rng`), Torch en CPU y en cada dispositivo CUDA y — a través de esos dos — Cellpose, de modo que la mezcla de campos, las particiones de folds y la inicialización de Cellpose se repiten entre ejecuciones con la misma semilla. sklearn no tiene ninguna semilla global; :func:`random_state` es lo que pasan los puntos donde se construyen estimadores. Lo que no puede hacerse determinista se enumera en :attr:`SeedReport.caveats` y en el docstring de :func:`seed_everything`.

records.context: **One error policy, honoured at every batch boundary.** ``on_error`` is a tri-state, default ``"stop"``:
records.label: spacr.runctx#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **One error policy, honoured at every batch boundary.** ``on_error`` is a tri-state, default ``"stop"``:
records.translation: **Una política de errores, respetada en cada frontera de lote.** ``on_error`` es un triestado, por defecto ``"stop"``:

records.context: ``stop`` the first failed unit aborts the processing session. The default, because a workflow that quietly drops a third of its plates produces a number that looks exactly like a good one. ``skip`` the unit is recorded — on the :class:`~spacr.errors.RunLedger` *and* as a :class:`SkipRecord` naming the unit, the stage and why — and the processing session carries on. Never a silent drop: :attr:`ErrorPolicy.skips` is what was lost. ``retry`` the unit is attempted :attr:`ErrorPolicy.attempts` times with an exponential backoff, and if the budget runs out it behaves exactly like ``stop``.
records.label: spacr.runctx#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``stop`` the first failed unit aborts the run. The default, because a pipeline that quietly drops a third of its plates produces a number that looks exactly like a good one. ``skip`` the unit is recorded — on the :class:`~spacr.errors.RunLedger` *and* as a :class:`SkipRecord` naming the unit, the stage and why — and the run carries on. Never a silent drop: :attr:`ErrorPolicy.skips` is what was lost. ``retry`` the unit is attempted :attr:`ErrorPolicy.attempts` times with an exponential backoff, and if the budget runs out it behaves exactly like ``stop``.
records.translation: ``stop``: la primera unidad que falla aborta la ejecución. Es el valor por defecto, porque un pipeline que descarta discretamente un tercio de sus placas produce un número que parece exactamente uno bueno. ``skip``: la unidad se registra — en el :class:`~spacr.errors.RunLedger` *y* como un :class:`SkipRecord` que nombra la unidad, la etapa y el motivo — y la ejecución continúa. Nunca es un descarte silencioso: :attr:`ErrorPolicy.skips` es lo que se perdió. ``retry``: la unidad se intenta :attr:`ErrorPolicy.attempts` veces con espera exponencial, y si se agota el presupuesto se comporta exactamente como ``stop``.

Classify (ML) had two, and chose between them **implicitly**: ``ml.py`` asked whether ``annotation_column`` was ``None``. records.translation: **La base de entrenamiento.** Classify (CV) ya tenía las tres: ``dataset_mode`` es ``'metadata'``, ``'annotation'`` o ``'measurement'``, y :mod:`spacr.io` construye el conjunto de datos a partir de ``class_metadata``/``metadata_rules`` o ``annotation_columns``/``annotation_values`` según corresponda. records.context: **Backward compatibility.** A settings CSV written before this exists in every user's project folder, and, as INVARIANTS §6 records, a structured-data name *absent* from the key-value mapping means the workflow falls back to its own default, which can differ from the GUI's, and nothing says so.
